newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 8.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- SING TAO said passengers had contributed to the Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp's profits and were entitled to better treatment than paying unreasonably high fares. The paper suggested that a committee be set up by the government to decide fare increases, and not to let KCRC decide everything on its own.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said if the "one country, two systems" policy could work in Hong Kong, it could also solve the Taiwan issue. The paper said that despite the reluctance of its government now, Taiwan would eventually adopt the "one country two systems" policy. Reunification was a historical trend and its realisation was just a matter of time, and it was not up to Taiwan authorities to choose, the paper said.

-- HONG KONG STANDARD said everybody's interests would be served if the Court of Appeal could immediately listen to arguments regarding the legality of the provisional legislature from all sides and deliver its findings as early as possible. Hong Kong could not afford to have this issue as a sword of Democles hanging over the heads of the executive, the legislature and even members of the Bench, the paper said.
